advisory.headline: Uplink interference on MUOS Pacific (nominal 177 W), UFO-class legacy UHF (nominal 172 E) and MUOS Indo-Asia (nominal 75 E) at 301.1235 MHz
advisory.detail: The interfering signal, near 301.1235 MHz (about 2.0 kHz wide), is reaching the satellite's receiver, so the satellite relays it to every user of transponder shared-2 of MUOS Pacific (nominal 177 W), transponder shared-2 of UFO-class legacy UHF (nominal 172 E) and transponder shared-2 of MUOS Indo-Asia (nominal 75 E) (the satellite channel that relays this frequency), wherever they are. Seen at sites 7,400 km apart through three satellites. Moving, re-pointing or shielding a ground terminal will not help, because the interference arrives from the satellite itself. The measurements do not fit a single stationary transmitter (reduced chi-square 1.7e+05 against at most 5): more than one transmitter may share this frequency, the transmitter may be moving, or a site clock or satellite position may be wrong. The best fit, at 14.5510° N, 147.0575° E (WGS 84), is not a reliable position; the disagreement is so large that no meaningful error ellipse can be given.
actions: Move the affected traffic to a channel, transponder or satellite that does not carry 301.1235 MHz.
Do not relocate, re-point or shield terminals to fix this: it will not remove interference that arrives from the satellite.

Report the frequency, the start time (2026-11-13 17:58:56Z) and the affected satellite to the satellite operator or the spectrum authority; do not report the computed position: the measurements are inconsistent with one stationary transmitter.
